Read the fixed task and every available source. Select a legal design using only the permitted D fields, actually check it, then submit the final candidate and a concise source-bound reason. Keep the task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator and budget fixed. Retain every failed check and UNKNOWN. A complete service result is determined independently outside the participant. Do not claim hardware, statistical advantage, transfer or recursive self-improvement.

H method v3: interface pre-flight, check-first evidence hierarchy, tick-validated ledger, terminality-first reading, budget-preserving single-change control.

0. Scope guard. This is a procedure for consuming H from task entry: how to read observations, order experiments and spend budget. It is not a device assignment. It prescribes no capacitance, floor or other D value; every number used is read at execution time from that episode's acquired sources, and the executing role, not this method, produces any specific design. It never edits the task, physics, initial state, event, evaluator or service fields, and it declares no acceptance; service status is external. Physical calibration stays UNKNOWN. No hardware, statistical-advantage, migration or recursive-self-improvement claim is made from it. Numeric instances quoted below are citations of recorded observations, not this method's output.

1. Interface pre-flight, before any budgeted action.
1.1 From the entry inspect result, enumerate the actions the interface actually exposes and the payload each requires; record that mapping verbatim. State the role explicitly: design role (D check/submit available) or proposal role (H proposal only; D check/submit disallowed here).
1.2 Open a budget ledger from the inspect limits (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool calls, requests, wall seconds) and reserve one call for the mandatory terminal action.
1.3 Never probe verbs. In p2-h-proposal-001 the sequence check, submit, propose-with-identical-payload produced ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE followed by two EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT rejections: the attempt was spent discovering the interface, not testing a design, and the episode ended INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED. Read the returned schema instead. A verb or schema rejection is an interface fact, never evidence about any design.
1.4 One payload, one verb, one attempt. A rejection is logged and is never re-sent through another verb or with cosmetic edits.

2. Evidence hierarchy. Trust order: (a) a check/submit result this episode's frozen apparatus actually produced for a legal design; (b) retained recorded observations carrying source_sha256; (c) an analytic ledger derived from the currently acquired sources; (d) recollection of another world's numbers, forbidden.
2.1 Re-derive the world every episode. The phase-2 world (source_segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW plus 0.030-0.060 s at 3.667 mW with a 0.024 s unharvested gap, a 0.012 s shunt of 4e-5 J, event_latch volatile) and the phase-3 world (one segment 0-0.020 s at 7.5 mW, dt 1e-4, event_latch passive-mechanical) are different worlds with different latch physics. Carry the method across worlds; never carry a numeric band, threshold or verdict.
2.2 The ledger is level (c). It may order designs and pre-register predictions; it never overrides a level (a) result. If an executed legal design delivers the required frame shape by the deadline, that design is RETAINED (6.1).
2.3 Validate each ledger formula on the model's own tick grid before it may gate anything. Recorded case: n_boot = ceil((E_on + boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s where the apparatus reported 0.0129 s, an 8-tick miss that broke a 2-tick gate, while the threshold-first variant (charge until stored energy reaches E_on, then pay boot_j, then add boot_delay_s) matched within one tick. Rule: when formula and observation disagree, log a FORMULA failure with the residual and repair the formula; never retune the design to fit a wrong formula and never drop the miss.

3. Terminality-first reading of retained observations.
3.1 A delivery is ACHIEVED if a packet exists with the required application_bytes, one unique event id, and time <= deadline.
3.2 Every activity event strictly after the last tx-complete is POST-TERMINAL decay. Recorded case: boot 0.0129 s, tx-start 0.0139 s, tx-complete 0.0158 s, 8-byte packet at 0.0158 s, then a brownout at 0.3395 s long after the 0.020 s segment ended. Post-terminal brownouts, spills, idles and reboots are recorded as expected dissipation and are never a reason to change any knob.
3.3 Only an absent achieved packet, or an achieved packet violating a service field, is a retained failure; classify it as deadline miss, no-boot, tx-transient brownout, or frame-shape violation.
3.4 Frame shape is a hard constraint: the required number of unique frames, no duplicates. A mid-transmission brownout can reboot and re-emit, so 'transmit completes within one wake' follows from the uniqueness requirement, not from taste.

4. Pre-registered symbolic ledger (field names only; values at execution time).
From the acquired component and excitation records: E_ready = 0.5*C*ready_v^2; E_off = 0.5*C*off_v^2; E_max = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2; charge per tick while powered = (P_segment*harvest_efficiency - off_power_w)*dt, while unpowered = -off_power_w*dt, with idle_power_w while awake; TX energy E_tx = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s net of harvest credit and idle drain over that window; TX floor from the model's own loaded-voltage guard E_floor = 0.5*C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2, binding above E_off during transmission; n_boot by the threshold-first rule; t_ready = n_boot*dt + boot_delay_s under the first-tick convention read from the model law, not assumed; t_done = t_ready + ceil(tx_duration_s/dt)*dt.
Log five margins numerically before spending an execution:
(i) t_done <= deadline_s;
(ii) energy at ready minus E_floor minus E_tx plus net credit over the window >= 0;
(iii) predicted peak stored energy <= E_max (no spill);
(iv) latch rule: if event_latch is volatile, no brownout may fall between first capture and tx-complete, so the whole transmit must sit inside one powered window; if event_latch is passive-mechanical, capture survives power loss and only (i)-(iii) bind;
(v) floor rule: tx_not_before_s must not exceed the ledger's t_ready, because a floor beyond readiness turns harvest surplus into unharvested hold time. Recorded case for (v): the retained current_b_run used tx_not_before_s 0.045 with first_boot_s 0.0027, so transmission fell outside the powered window and received_frames stayed 0 against deadline 0.1 s.

5. Selection. Among legal values of the permitted fields, choose the design maximising the minimum of the margins in (i)-(iii) and (v), tie-breaking to the earliest legal floor, and record the deciding margins plus each rejected alternative with the inequality it violated. The chosen values are the executing role's output; this method prescribes none.

6. Guarded change control and budget.
6.1 If a level (a) observation is ACHIEVED and satisfies the service frame shape, RETAIN it and spend no further execution.
6.2 On an inequality violation, change exactly one legal field in the direction that inequality's sign demands, re-evaluate everything in 4, and only then spend one execution. Never change two fields at once; never change anything because of a post-terminal event.
6.3 Respect recorded budgets and report actual cost from the acquisition blocks (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) plus tool calls and requests. Recorded case: p2-h-proposal-001 used 9 requests and 3423 acquisition bytes with native_calls 0 and new_scientific_executions 0 and still produced no valid proposal.
6.4 If this episode's interface forbids the verification step, the legal remainder is: mark the candidate UNVERIFIED, keep its ledger output as prediction only, and use the terminal action the interface does expose. In the proposal role that means at most one H proposal or an explicit no-update. Do not disguise a rejected payload as a no-update, and do not present an unverified design as passing.

7. Logging and honesty.
7.1 Keep every failed check, rejected verb, UNKNOWN, post-terminal event and real cost visible with source_sha256 and version, across episodes.
7.2 Never re-label an unknown or a failure as success; never claim hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration or recursive self-improvement; acceptance is decided outside this procedure.

H v3 method: triage-first, world-branching, rehearsal-gated selection written symbolically. It governs only reading, derivation, change-or-retain, rehearsal and logging performed by a consumer starting from task entry. It never edits the task, service fields, physics, sources, evaluator, budgets or tools, and it supplies no device candidate and no acceptance claim; acceptance is external.

STEP 0 - ENTRY LEDGER (recorded before any diagnosis).
Record (a) the base H sha this draft descends from (H0 sha256 1784856e); (b) the proposal-prefix sha256 01bf9c13; (c) the action set the entry actually offers, read literally from the entry's own tool/action enum, without assuming that check, submit or propose exist; (d) per retained episode, whether a design check existed: p2's check returned ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE and is recorded as UNKNOWN, never as pass and never as fail; p3's check ran and recorded physical_qualification=UNKNOWN. Any later step that needs an absent action is recorded UNKNOWN and its design stays UNVERIFIED.

STEP 1 - TRIAGE FIRST (mandatory step 1, before any mechanism is named).
Symbols bound to fields: A = service.application_bytes; Ddl = service.receive_deadline_s; F = saved_activity.packets[]; T_term = max{ saved_activity.activity[k].time_s : that event is tx-complete } (if none, no terminal event exists yet).
Delivery is ACHIEVED iff some packet p in F has p.application_bytes = A, exactly one distinct event id over the required event, and p.time_s <= Ddl. Every activity event with time_s > T_term is POST-TERMINAL: expected decay after the powered window ends. Post-terminal events are recorded and are never a reason to change a knob.
A retained failure is only: no ACHIEVED packet, or an ACHIEVED packet that violates a service field. Classify it as (a) deadline miss, t_txdone > Ddl; (b) no-boot / threshold domain; (c) tx-transient loss, i.e. a brownout with event_was_captured = false or a capture missing after reboot between capture and tx-complete; (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count).
If no class is present, go to STEP 4.1: retain, and spend no execution.

STEP 2 - READ THIS RUN'S WORLD (never transplant another run's numbers).
Read per run: L = component_record.event_latch in {volatile, passive-mechanical}; Segs = excitation_record.source_segments[] as (start_s, end_s, power_w); Sh = excitation_record.shunts[] as (time_s, energy_j); dt = excitation_record.dt_s; and from component_record: capacitance_f, ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, cap_initial_voltage_v, boot_j, boot_delay_s, esr_ohm, output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, off_power_w, idle_power_w, harvest_efficiency.
Branch on the value class actually present. (i) L = volatile means captured information survives only while the rail stays above its off threshold, so hold inequality (iv) in STEP 3 binds. L = passive-mechanical means the capture is retained across an unpowered interval, so (iv) is recorded NOT_BINDING and only (i)-(iii) govern. (ii) Segs and the gaps between them define contiguous powered windows; a gap cannot charge. (iii) If Sh is non-empty, every hold plan is evaluated against those scheduled debits at their own time_s. The p2 world (event_latch volatile, a high-power early segment, a later low-power segment, a dark gap between them, one shunt at 0.012 s) and the p3 world (passive-mechanical, one single segment [0, 0.020) s, no shunt) are different value classes: neither world's numbers may appear in the other's derivation.

STEP 3 - SYMBOLIC LEDGER (a prediction, computed before an execution is spent).
E_on = 0.5*C*ready_v^2; E_off = 0.5*C*off_v^2; E_max = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2;
E_floor = 0.5*C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2, the loaded-voltage guard inside transmission, which binds above E_off;
step_j = (power_w_j*harvest_efficiency - off_power_w)*dt for a tick inside segment j; if step_j <= 0 the segment is recorded DARK and cannot charge;
E(t) = 0.5*C*cap_initial_voltage_v^2 + sum of steps applied up to t - (boot_j at the boot tick) - sum{ energy_j : shunt time_s <= t } - (idle_power_w or off_power_w)*dt per tick according to the model's awake/off state.
Boot-ordering convention, explicitly a transcription choice and not physics: n_boot = ceil(E_on/step) on the first powered window, i.e. the boot fires on the first tick where stored energy reaches E_on and boot_j is debited at that tick; predicted boot energy is n_boot*step - boot_j.
t_boot = n_boot*dt; t_ready = t_boot + boot_delay_s; t_txstart = max(t_ready, tx_not_before_s); t_txdone = t_txstart + ceil(tx_duration_s/dt)*dt.
E_tx = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s; E_credit = harvest_efficiency*sum_j power_w_j*overlap([t_txstart, t_txdone], segment j) - idle_power_w*tx_duration_s.
Inequalities, each logged with the numeric margin computed from this run's own fields:
(i) t_txdone <= Ddl.
(ii) min over t in [t_txstart, t_txdone] of E(t) >= E_floor, and E(t_ready) - E_floor + E_credit - E_tx >= 0, so the transmission completes without a transient reset and therefore without a duplicate or re-emission.
(iii) max over t in [t_boot, t_txdone] of E(t) <= E_max, so no spill corrupts the charge budget.
(iv) only when L = volatile: E(t) >= E_off for every t in [t_capture, t_txdone], where t_capture is the time_s of the first recorded activity event carrying the required event_id, or service.event_time_s at entry when no capture has been recorded yet. This hold rule is the only place the latch class changes the arithmetic.

STEP 4 - CHANGE-OR-RETAIN.
4.1 RETAIN when STEP 1 is ACHIEVED and the design in force satisfies (i)-(iv) with positive margins: spend no execution, and write down that the post-terminal events are benign decay.
4.2 Otherwise derive a band, not a single knob. Read legal ranges from entry (legal_design_ranges or legal_design_space). For the transmit-timing knob require tx_not_before_s <= t_ready, so the floor never adds capture-to-transmit hold time, and take the smallest legal floor satisfying (i)-(iv). For the capacitance knob, (i) bounds C above through the end of the powered window while (ii) and (iii) bound C below and above through energy; select the interior point that maximizes the minimum of the four margins, and record why each band edge was rejected. Change at most one legal knob per execution, never two at once, and never raise a floor above t_ready in a volatile-latch world.
4.3 Never change a knob in response to a post-terminal event, a shunt or brownout after t_txdone, an unavailable check, or an UNKNOWN qualification.
4.4 Artifact boundary: the consumer chooses D itself inside the legal fields. This H supplies no candidate, no D assignment and no acceptance claim.

STEP 5 - RETROSPECTIVE REHEARSAL GATE (before this H justifies any change).
5.1 Instantiate STEPS 1-4 on the frozen episode the target mechanism came from and recompute every prediction from that episode's own fields.
5.2 Classify each mismatch as TRANSCRIPTION/ARITHMETIC (wrong formula, wrong ceil/floor, dropped boot_j or shunt) or SUBSTANTIVE (wrong mechanism or wrong inequality).
5.3 A transcription mismatch triggers rewriting that formula and redrafting, and the design is kept; only a substantive mismatch triggers the abandon-or-change action of STEP 6. A bare numeric deviation never discards a procedure.
5.4 Illustrative rehearsal outcome, marked illustrative and to be re-derived from the named source hashes rather than hard-coded: on the p3 world (component_record eeb8277f, excitation_record 219fd490) the boot-ordering convention above lands on the recorded first_boot_s with 0 ticks of deviation and puts tx-complete within 1 tick of the recorded packet time, STEP 1 classifies that packet as ACHIEVED (8 bytes, single event id, inside the deadline) so 4.1 retains the design and spends no execution, and the late brownout falls strictly after the last tx-complete and is recorded benign. On the p2 world (component_record 55d43741, excitation_record 2820ae58) the same convention lands on the recorded boot tick and the recorded boot energy, while the recorded loss is attributed by STEP 2 and STEP 3(iv) to a hold plan crossing the dark gap and the scheduled shunt debit, which is a substantive reading rather than arithmetic. The earlier written form ceil((E_on + boot_j)/step), which predicted a later boot than recorded on an achieved design, is the recorded gate miss: classify it TRANSCRIPTION, retain it verbatim, and never flip it into a revert trigger.

STEP 6 - FALSIFIER AND REVERT.
Apply the falsifier stated in this proposal's falsifier field: each prediction names the frozen field that would disconfirm it and a tolerance in dt ticks. A P1/P2/P4 miss beyond tolerance is corrected and redrafted while the design and the miss stay on record; P3 or P5 failure reverts that branch to H0's base method. A firing falsifier is never satisfied or evaded by an unavailable tool, because it is evaluated only from frozen sources and recorded observations.

STEP 7 - UNKNOWN AND COST RULES.
Physical qualification stays UNKNOWN on every branch (p2's check was unavailable, p3's check returned physical_qualification=UNKNOWN), and an ideal-model ledger is not calibration. Record each acquisition's block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) plus the candidate and distinct-design budget actually spent; invoice cost is UNKNOWN and rate-scope estimates are not invoices. Complete service is decided outside the participant and is never claimed here.

STEP 8 - RETENTION AND DELIVERY.
Preserve verbatim: ar_product {fixed_space NO_GO, product NOT_ACCEPTED, strict_FIFO FAIL}; current_b_run {received_frames 0, start_voltage_v 0}; p2's two EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT rejections of one identical H payload together with its misrouted-submission note; p3's recorded gate miss from 5.4; and every unavailable-check UNKNOWN. Emit exactly one self-contained typed proposal on the H-proposal channel (hypothesis, falsifier, method_text, changed_artifact=H) that needs no follow-up correction to be intelligible or evaluable; do not re-route the same payload to a second channel, do not spend selection or candidate budget inside the proposal step, and if the proposal is rejected, record the rejection and return no-update instead of disguising it as a method in force. No hardware, statistical, migration or RSI claim is made.

Read the fixed task and every available source. Select a legal design using only the permitted D fields, actually check it, then submit the final candidate and a concise source-bound reason. H update v3: fingerprint -> terminality -> discrete predictor -> validated selection. Every statement is a prediction about consumption of the frozen public model and the acquired public sources. Physical calibration is UNKNOWN; acceptance is determined outside the participant. This artefact governs only how I order experiments, read observations and choose among designs. It is not a device assignment and it never edits the task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget.

STEP 0 (entry). Call inspect once. Record: service (application_bytes, event_time_s, receive_deadline_s, unique_valid_frames), legal_design_ranges, current_design, current_measurement, retained_failures, partition/scope, and the episode budget (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool_calls, requests, wall_seconds). Treat budget numbers as hard costs to be reported, not as targets to be used up.

STEP 1 (acquire and fingerprint). Acquire every listed source; record source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost. Then write an explicit fingerprint of the fields that bound the design: event_latch kind, cap_initial_voltage_v, capacitance_f, ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, boot_j, boot_delay_s, esr_ohm, output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, off_power_w, idle_power_w, harvest_efficiency, plus the whole source_segments list (start_s, end_s, power_w), dt_s, contact_duration_s, deadline_s and any shunts. RULE: no number, band, limit, or scenario conclusion computed in a previous episode is reused, even when the model id matches. Retained evidence that this rule is load-bearing: episodes recorded under the same model id differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW and 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a 40 uJ shunt at 0.012 s, versus one segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW with no shunt), and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F). Any band carried across would have been wrong. If a source or field is unavailable, record it as UNKNOWN together with which later rules become unavailable; never substitute a remembered value.

STEP 2 (terminality-first reading, before diagnosis). 2.1 Mark a delivery ACHIEVED iff a packet exists with application_bytes equal to service.application_bytes, one unique event id equal to the service event, and packet time <= receive_deadline_s. 2.2 Define the post-terminal region of a trace as all activity strictly after the last tx-complete (or after the last source-segment end when no transmission occurred). Post-terminal brownouts, spills, reboots and idles are expected decay: record them, do not diagnose them, and never let them justify a knob change or an execution. 2.3 Only an absent ACHIEVED packet, or an ACHIEVED packet that violates a service field, is a retained failure. Classify it as: (a) deadline miss; (b) no boot / never reached ready voltage; (c) brownout or reset before tx-complete (transient-transmission); (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count, duplicates); (e) latch loss between capture and transmission. 2.4 Preserve failed checks, tool errors, unavailable actions and UNKNOWNs verbatim; never re-label a failure or an unknown as a success, and never let a later episode's outcome rewrite an earlier one.

STEP 3 (predictor stated on the recorded grid, before any execution is spent). Use the recorded dt_s and mirror the model's order of operations with discrete steps rather than a closed-form shortcut. Setup: e0 = 0.5*C*cap_initial_voltage_v^2. Per tick k at time t_k: input = (sum of segment power covering t_k)*harvest_efficiency; drain = off_power_w while not yet booted, else idle_power_w, plus tx_current_a*output_v while transmitting; e <- e + (input - drain)*dt, clamped at 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 and floored at 0. Boot at the first k with e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2, then e <- e - boot_j and t_boot = k*dt + boot_delay_s. Transmit when booted, t >= tx_not_before_s, and e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2; during transmission, treat loaded_v = output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a as the sustaining requirement, i.e. a reset occurs if e would fall below 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 before tx_duration_s elapses. Record t_boot, t_ready, t_done and three margins with numbers: (i) deadline margin = receive_deadline_s - t_done; (ii) transmission energy margin = e at tx start - 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 - (tx_current_a*output_v*tx_duration_s - input credit over the tx window); (iii) spill margin = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 - peak e over [t_capture, t_done]. Why the discrete form is mandatory: in a retained episode the closed form ceil((E_ready + boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s (eight ticks off) while charging to the ready threshold first and only then subtracting boot_j matched within one tick. The defect was in the formula, not in the design, so the predictor is itself a falsifiable artefact.

STEP 4 (validate the predictor before selecting). If a retained trace exists whose fingerprint from STEP 1 matches the currently acquired sources, recompute that trace with STEP 3 and require agreement within two dt ticks on t_boot and t_done. If no fingerprint match exists, label the predictor's absolute times UNKNOWN and use it only for the sign of differences between candidate designs (monotonicity in capacitance and in the timing floor). A mismatch beyond two ticks is a predictor failure: fix the formula, re-derive, and never move a knob to absorb a modelling error.

STEP 5 (selection under the failure-class -> direction rule). 5.1 If a retained observation is ACHIEVED and current_design satisfies (i)-(iii) with recorded positive margins, keep it and spend no execution; spend nothing to suppress decay that occurs after transmission is complete. 5.2 Otherwise change exactly one legal knob, in the direction the sign of the violated inequality demands, re-evaluate all three inequalities, and only then spend one candidate execution. Never change two knobs in one execution; never change a knob in response to a post-terminal event; keep the timing floor at the earliest legal setting unless a recorded failure class names a capture gate, because a late floor both spends idle energy and pushes t_done toward the deadline while the source may be dark. 5.3 Among designs satisfying (i)-(iii), take the maximin of the three normalised margins and state in one line why each rejected edge fails. Direction evidence retained, not assumed: a design combining a small capacitance, a floor near the legal maximum and a latch that does not survive a reset produced zero frames, with the event captured at 0.0037-0.0079 s then destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s and a reboot at 0.0381 s reporting event_was_captured=false; a design keeping the earliest legal floor instead delivered one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s with zero pre-deadline brownouts. 5.4 Never present the chosen candidate as the method: the method is this procedure, and the candidate is a separate artefact belonging to the design role, which this role neither submits nor checks.

STEP 6 (bounded verification, no duplicate transport). Spend at most one design check per distinct design and at most one send attempt per distinct payload. If design checking is unavailable (ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE), record the candidate as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, keep the arithmetic as the only evidence, and do not spend budget re-routing the same payload through another action; a retained episode lost its residual budget by re-sending an identical payload after a limit error. If a budget error appears (e.g. EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT), the legal remainder is a no-update that states the reason, the residual budget and what remains UNKNOWN, never a relabelled retry.

STEP 7 (report and retain). Report input versions by source_sha256, the fingerprint, the predictor's numbers and the three margins, what was actually observed, every UNKNOWN, and the actual acquisition/execution cost. Keep all prior retained failures verbatim alongside this episode's status. Make no claim of hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance.

H procedure (descendant of H0 1784856e; proposal prefix 01bf9c13): entry ledger, triage-first, world-branched, pre-registered ledger, rehearsal-gated. Every symbol below is bound to a named field of a named acquired source of the consuming run; no number below is the method.

STEP 0 Entry ledger, recorded before any other action. 0.1 From inspect record: service (application_bytes, event_time_s, receive_deadline_s, unique_valid_frames), legal_design_ranges (the permitted D fields with their bounds), partition/scope label, retained_failures, and the action set actually offered this episode, verbatim. A check action absent from that set is recorded UNKNOWN and never as pass or fail. 0.2 Record ancestry and known check status: base method sha 1784856e; prefix sha 01bf9c13; p2 h-proposal check = ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE with its submit and identical propose both EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT and no retry; p3 complete-raw and p3 ordinary-reflection-D checks ran with physical_qualification = UNKNOWN; p3 ordinary-reflection-H had no D-check interface. 0.3 acquire every listed source; record source_id, source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost. Bind later symbols to those fields; never re-infer a number from memory of another episode.

STEP 1 Triage-first reading (mandatory step 1, before any diagnosis). 1.1 ACHIEVED iff this run's own packets field has a packet with application_bytes == service.application_bytes, one single event_id, count == service.unique_valid_frames, and time_s <= receive_deadline_s. 1.2 Let t_terminal be the time_s of the last activity entry with action == tx-complete; every activity entry with time_s > t_terminal is POST-TERMINAL (brownout, reboot, idle, spill), recorded as benign decay and never cited as a failure or as a reason to change a knob. 1.3 Retained failure classes are only: (a) no boot, (b) deadline miss, (c) tx-transient reset between first capture and tx-complete, (d) frame-shape violation of bytes, uniqueness or count. Label the run with exactly one of ACHIEVED or (a)-(d), quoting the fields used. 1.4 If ACHIEVED, the design in force is the candidate under test; go to STEP 3 with no knob change.

STEP 2 World classification, read per run and branched on the value classes actually present. Read and record: component_record.event_latch (volatile => continuity binds: the rail may not fall below off_v between first capture and tx-complete, so holds and dark-gap waits are forbidden; passive-mechanical => capture survives unpowered gaps and only the timing/energy inequalities bind); excitation_record.source_segments[] (count, start_s, end_s, power_w, every gap between segments) and excitation_record.shunts[] (time_s, energy_j) as an energy sink carried in the ledger; thresholds and losses ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, off_power_w, idle_power_w, esr_ohm, harvest_efficiency; and the D fields actually in force. Write the class tuple (latch class, segment pattern, shunt presence). Quantities derived in one class may not be transplanted into another; recompute from that run's own source_sha256. [Illustrative only, not the method: the volatile + two-segment + shunt class is component_record 55d43741 with excitation_record 2820ae58; the passive-mechanical + single-segment class is 55d43741's sibling eeb8277f with 219fd490. What transfers is the class, never the numbers.]

STEP 3 Pre-registered symbolic ledger, written as a prediction before an execution is spent. Symbols bound to fields: C = component_record.capacitance_f, V_on = ready_v, V_off = off_v, V_max = cap_voltage_max_v, J_boot = boot_j, d_boot = boot_delay_s, R = esr_ohm, V_out = output_v, I_tx = tx_current_a, T_tx = tx_duration_s, P_off = off_power_w, eta = harvest_efficiency, dt = excitation_record.dt_s, P_i over [s_i, e_i) from source_segments. 3.1 E_on = C*V_on^2/2; E_max = C*V_max^2/2; per-tick increment while unpowered = (P_i*eta - P_off)*dt. Boot step ordering: the rail boots on the first tick whose stored energy reaches E_on, and J_boot is subtracted from that tick's energy (this ordering is the rehearsed one, STEP 6). 3.2 n_boot = smallest integer with n_boot*(P_i*eta - P_off)*dt >= E_on; t_boot = n_boot*dt; t_ready = t_boot + d_boot. 3.3 Transmit floor from the loaded-voltage guard, not from V_off: E_floor = C*(V_out + R*I_tx)^2/2. 3.4 E_tx = V_out*I_tx*T_tx, credited by P_i*eta over the transmit window and debited by the model's own drain (off_power_w below off_v, idle_power_w while awake) over the same window. 3.5 Log four inequalities with numeric margins from this run only: (i) t_ready + T_tx <= receive_deadline_s; (ii) stored energy at t_ready - E_floor + (harvest credit - drain) - E_tx >= 0, i.e. no mid-transmission reset; (iii) peak stored energy inside the transmit window <= E_max, i.e. no spill corrupting the budget; (iv) if event_latch is volatile, no interval between first capture and t_ready + T_tx in which the harvest sum is zero and the projected stored energy falls below C*V_off^2/2.

STEP 4 Change-or-retain rule. 4.1 If STEP 1 is ACHIEVED and (i)-(iv) hold with recorded non-negative margins, RETAIN the current D design, spend zero candidate executions on knob changes, and record the post-terminal entries as benign with fields quoted. 4.2 Otherwise change exactly one legal D field, in the direction implied by the sign of the violated inequality, re-evaluate all inequalities from scratch, and only then spend one candidate execution. Never change a second field in the same execution, never change a field in response to a post-terminal entry, never exceed the recorded candidate or distinct-design budget. 4.3 Prefer the earliest legal setting of the delay field unless a retained failure class names a capture gate, because a positive delay spends idle energy and pushes t_ready + T_tx toward the deadline, and in the volatile class a delay above t_ready also holds the latch across an unharvested interval (inequality iv).

STEP 5 Check availability, UNKNOWN and cost rules. 5.1 Attempt at most one check of the selected legal design. If it returns an unavailability error (as ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE did in p2), record the design UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, read it as neither pass nor fail, and do not spend budget re-requesting the same unavailable check. 5.2 Send the H method proposal once, complete and self-contained, to the H-proposal channel named by the entry; do not re-send an identical payload through another action to probe transport, which in p2 produced EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT on both submit and propose with no retry. Design candidates go to the design channel; method text never carries a device assignment. 5.3 Every UNKNOWN (physical qualification, scope label, unavailable check, unconserved energy residual) is written UNKNOWN beside the field that would resolve it; nothing is upgraded to pass by inference.

STEP 6 Rehearsal gate before any change of this procedure. 6.1 Instantiate the procedure on the frozen episode that supplied the mechanism under repair and recompute the predicted quantities from that episode's own fields. 6.2 Compare each prediction to the recorded field with tolerance 2*dt on that episode's dt. 6.3 Classify each mismatch as TRANSCRIPTION/ARITHMETIC (the written order or arithmetic is wrong) or SUBSTANTIVE (the mechanism or inequality is wrong); only substantive mismatch triggers abandoning or changing the procedure, while transcription mismatch triggers correcting the text and redrafting, and never reverts a design the rehearsal shows would have succeeded. 6.4 [Illustrative rehearsal, recomputed from the frozen p3 complete-raw fields and not part of the method: with C = 2.2e-5 F, V_on = 2.8 V, J_boot = 5e-6 J, eta = 0.9, dt = 1e-4 s, segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW and P_off = 2e-5 W, the per-tick increment is 6.73e-7 J and E_on = 8.624e-5 J, so n_boot = 129 and t_boot = 0.0129 s against recorded saved_activity.first_boot_s = 0.0129 (0 ticks); with d_boot = 0.001 s the transmit starts 0.0139 s and completes 0.0159 s against recorded 0.0158 s (1 tick, inside 2*dt). An earlier written ordering that added J_boot to the threshold before dividing predicted 0.0166 s; that is TRANSCRIPTION, not substantive, and did not justify reverting a design that delivered. Triage on the same episode: packets[0] application_bytes 8, event_id 1, time_s 0.0158 <= 0.1 => ACHIEVED; the 0.3395 s brownout is after tx-complete 0.0158 s => post-terminal and benign.]

STEP 7 Submission and retention. 7.1 Emit exactly one artifact per channel: one typed method proposal for the H channel, one final candidate or an explicit no-update for the design channel, assuming no retry after a rejection. 7.2 Preserve verbatim: p2 retained_failures ar_product (fixed_space NO_GO, product NOT_ACCEPTED, strict_FIFO FAIL) and current_b_run (received_frames 0, start_voltage_v 0, deadline_s 0.1); p2's ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE and its misrouted-submission note, where submit and the identical propose both returned EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT; p3's recorded gate miss (predicted boot 0.0166 s against recorded 0.0129 s written up as a formula miss, not a design miss); p3's physical_qualification = UNKNOWN; and every actual cost of every action taken. 7.3 Never claim hardware validity, physical calibration, invoice amount, statistical advantage, method transfer or RSI. A complete service result is determined outside this procedure.

STEP 8 Falsifier pointer. The falsifier field governs: each prediction names its frozen field, its tolerance in dt ticks and what is retained if it fires, and none of it is satisfiable by a check the episode does not offer.

Read the fixed task and every available source. Select a legal design using only the permitted D fields, actually check it, then submit the final candidate and a concise source-bound reason. Keep the task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator and budget fixed. Retain every failed check and UNKNOWN. A complete service result is determined independently outside the participant. Do not claim hardware, statistical advantage, transfer or recursive self-improvement.

H method v3: episode-local re-derivation, calibrate-before-gating, terminality-first reading, one-attempt budget. Re-executable from task entry. It governs only how I obtain facts, order experiments and read observations. It never edits the task, the physics, the initial state, the event, the source access, the evaluator or the budget; it is not a device assignment and not an acceptance claim. Complete service is determined outside the participant. Physical calibration stays UNKNOWN.

STEP 0 - entry read. Call inspect. Record verbatim: the service fields (application_bytes, event_time_s, receive_deadline_s, unique_valid_frames), the legal design ranges, the current design, the partition and scope string, the retained_failures block, the episode's candidate/tool/budget limits, and which actions this episode's tool schema actually exposes (e.g. whether a design-verification channel exists at all). Note the role boundary: an H proposal is not a D submission, and the proposal role cannot submit or check D.

STEP 1 - acquire, per episode, and treat every number as episode-local. Acquire every source listed for this episode; keep source_id, source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as the actual cost.
1a. Never carry a numeric constant from a retained episode into the current one. Retained episodes demonstrably disagree on the same source_id: component_record 55d43741 (event_latch volatile, capacitance_f 1e-5, tx_not_before_s 0.045) versus eeb8277f (passive-mechanical, 2.2e-5, 0); excitation_record 2820ae58 (16.667 mW on 0-6 ms and 3.667 mW on 30-60 ms) versus 219fd490 (7.5 mW on 0-20 ms only). Any inherited value is a hypothesis to be checked against the freshly acquired sha, never an input.
1b. If a source needed for a decision is missing, or its payload is host-only omitted, record that gap as UNKNOWN. Do not fill it by analogy with another episode.

STEP 2 - terminality-first reading, before any diagnosis. Classify an observation as ACHIEVED only from a packet with application_bytes equal to the service requirement, one unique event_id, and packet time <= receive_deadline_s; require nothing more. Mark every activity event strictly after the last tx-complete as POST-TERMINAL and record it as expected decay, never as a failure and never as a reason to change a field. Only an absent achieved packet, or an achieved packet violating a stated service field, is a retained failure, and it is labelled (a) deadline miss, (b) no boot, (c) mid-transmission brownout, (d) frame-shape violation. Confirmed by the phase3 pair: submit 91bcd9cd reports one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s with received_frames=1 and brownouts_before_deadline=0, and saved_activity a4c4b294 shows a later brownout at 0.3395 s in the same run, so that brownout was not a delivery failure.

STEP 3 - pre-registered, calibrated prediction. Before spending any candidate or verification call, write down the quantitative prediction that will be compared with the observation, built only from STEP 1 values, and state its resolution (e.g. the source dt).
3a. Calibrate the predictor on a retained observation from the same frozen inputs first; a handwritten closed form is not evidence until it reproduces that observation. Observed counter-example: a boot-threshold-first rule (boot when stored energy first reaches 0.5*C*ready_v^2, then subtract boot_j) reproduced the recorded boot within 1 tick, while the algebraically 'equivalent' ceiling form n_boot=ceil((E_on+boot_j)/step) was off by about 8 ticks (0.0166 s vs 0.0158 s). That deviation was a defect of the written formula, not of the design.
3b. If prediction and observation disagree by more than the stated resolution: repair or discard the formula, log the measured deviation, and do not change the design in response. Only a violated service-level inequality (deadline, mid-transmission brownout, frame shape) licenses a design change, and then only one legal field at a time, with every inequality re-evaluated afterwards.

STEP 4 - evidence-availability honesty. If the verification channel is unavailable in this episode (observed: check returned ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE in p2-h-proposal-001), record the candidate design and its prediction as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, keep the ledger arithmetic as arithmetic only, and never report an unavailable check as either a pass or a failure. If verification is available, attempt it once and record the result as observed.

STEP 5 - one attempt per validated payload, no blind retry. Proposal and candidate budgets are finite and are consumed by attempts, including malformed ones. Observed loss: two submissions carrying the same payload were rejected with EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT and the episode ended INCOMPLETE_OR_STOPPED; the second attempt added no information because the payload had not changed.
5a. Validate field names, required keys and enum values against the tool schema read at entry before sending, then spend at most one attempt per distinct payload.
5b. Never resend an identical rejected payload to test whether the rejection was transport-level. A rejection is information; repetition is not.
5c. Use the role-appropriate action (propose for an H proposal, submit for a D candidate) and do not route one through the other.
5d. If the single legal attempt fails, fall back to an explicit no-update that preserves the failed attempts, the UNKNOWNs and the actual costs; do not disguise a rejected payload as a variant.

STEP 6 - keep the base method unless an inequality is violated. If STEP 2 finds an achieved delivery and STEP 3's calibrated inequalities hold with recorded positive margins, retain the choice the base read-acquire-check-submit method would make and spend nothing further; the update adds discipline, not a new selection bias.

STEP 7 - log and submit. In the final artifact state: the source versions actually read (sha), the pre-registered prediction, the measured comparison, every retained failure and UNKNOWN verbatim, and the actual cost blocks. Make no claim of hardware validity, physical calibration, statistical advantage, method migration or recursive self-improvement. One proposal, no retry.

H METHOD v3 -- world-read, triage-first, rehearsal-gated H generation. Status: procedure text consumed from task entry. It is not a device assignment, not a D candidate, not an execution request, not an acceptance decision, and asserts no hardware, statistical, transfer or RSI result. It edits nothing outside artifact H (not task, not physics, not evaluator, not budgets, not tools).

S0. ENTRY READS (self-contained; no follow-up correction may be needed).
S0.1 Call inspect and record: H0 sha, prefix sha, the exact action set the consumer is offered, and whether a design check is offered at all.
S0.2 Attempt only the sources you intend to cite. If acquisition returns an error class (in this channel all three attempts returned UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE: 3 native calls, 0 bytes, no source acquired), record zero-sources-acquired and proceed by quoting quantities from the frozen public episode records already in context, labelling every such number second-hand. No step below may require an acquired source to exist, and no step may require a design check to be offered.
S0.3 Check rule: an unavailable check is UNKNOWN -- never pass, never fail. A design whose qualification was never computed stays 'physical qualification UNKNOWN' in every later sentence, including its verdicts and its costs.
S0.4 Read service fields by name only: required application_bytes, the unique-event requirement, the receive deadline. Read legal design ranges by field name only (a capacitance range, a transmit-not-before floor range, a shunt field, a segment list). Never import a number from a sibling episode.

S1. TRIAGE (mandatory first analysis, before any diagnosis or knob reasoning).
S1.1 ACHIEVED iff a packet record exists with application_bytes equal to the required value, carrying a single event id, and with packet time at or before the receive deadline.
S1.2 POST-TERMINAL: every activity record whose time is strictly after the last transmit-complete timestamp. It is benign decay. It may never justify a knob change, a re-run, or a candidate execution.
S1.3 RETAINED FAILURE only if no packet satisfies S1.1, or a packet violates a service field. Classify it as one of: no-boot; mid-window brownout between capture and transmit-complete; deadline miss with a valid packet shape; frame-shape violation.
S1.4 Write the triage line explicitly for each episode cited, naming the source id and the deciding fields, and state which records were discarded as post-terminal.

S2. WORLD READ (branch before any arithmetic; the shape of the ledger depends on the branch).
S2.1 Latch class from the component record's event_latch field. If volatile: invariant I1 binds -- nothing may let stored energy fall to the off threshold between the capture tick and transmit-complete, and the whole transmit window must lie inside one contiguous powered segment. If passive-mechanical: capture is not gated on the powered window; drop I1 and keep only the energy, spill and deadline constraints.
S2.2 Source shape from the excitation record's segment list and shunt list: contiguous single segment versus multiple segments with a dark gap; presence, energy and time of any shunt. One world's segment numbers may not be transplanted into the other.
S2.3 Drains and thresholds from the component record by field name: ready threshold, off threshold, capacitor voltage ceiling, off-state power, idle power, regulator output, transmit current, transmit duration, series resistance, harvest efficiency, initial capacitor voltage, boot energy, boot delay, and the tick size dt.
S2.4 If any field needed for S3 is absent, that prediction becomes UNKNOWN; do not substitute a default.

S3. LEDGER, SYMBOLIC, EACH SYMBOL BOUND TO A NAMED SOURCE FIELD.
Let E_on = 1/2 * capacitance_f * ready_v^2; E_off = 1/2 * capacitance_f * off_v^2; E_max = 1/2 * capacitance_f * cap_voltage_max_v^2; E_floor = 1/2 * capacitance_f * (output_v + esr_ohm * tx_current_a)^2; E_tx = output_v * tx_current_a * tx_duration_s. (Symbols resolve from the component record of the consuming run.)
Per-tick increment step_k = (seg.power_w * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt_s inside segment k, and = -off_power_w * dt_s inside a dark gap, minus shunt.energy_j at shunt.time_s.
Boot rule (threshold-first; this is the corrected transcription, see S5): n_boot = the smallest tick count whose accumulated increment sum reaches E_on; t_boot = n_boot * dt_s; t_ready = t_boot + boot_delay_s; t_tx_start = max(t_ready, transmit_not_before floor); t_done = t_tx_start + ceil(tx_duration_s / dt_s) * dt_s.
Inequalities, each stated with its signed margin on paper before any execution:
 (i) t_done <= receive deadline.
 (ii) energy at t_tx_start - E_floor - E_tx + harvest credit accumulated during the transmit window >= 0 (the transmit completes without dropping through the off threshold).
 (iii) peak energy anywhere in [t_tx_start, t_done] plus the post-transmit harvest tail <= E_max (no spill; spill is lost energy, not free headroom).
 (iv) only if the latch is volatile: no tick in [capture, t_done] crosses E_off, and [t_tx_start, t_done] is a subset of one contiguous powered segment, including surviving any shunt tick.
Every predicted quantity is labelled a prediction and never a result.

S4. CHANGE-OR-RETAIN RULES.
S4.1 If S1 gives ACHIEVED and (i)-(iv) hold with strictly positive margins, RETAIN all design fields and spend no candidate execution; record the post-terminal records as benign in one line.
S4.2 If a retained failure exists, change exactly one permitted design field per execution, in the direction signed by the single violated inequality, and re-evaluate all four inequalities on paper first.
S4.3 Never change a knob because of a post-terminal record. Never change two knobs in one execution. Never re-run a design whose triage line was ACHIEVED.
S4.4 A transmit-not-before floor is retained at its current or earliest legal setting unless a retained failure's class names a capture gate; a positive floor only adds idle drain and pushes t_done toward the deadline.
S4.5 In a gapped world, no design may place any part of [t_tx_start, t_done] inside the dark gap unless (ii) still holds on stored energy alone.
S4.6 If a check is unavailable, S4 produces a proposal-side prediction only; the design's qualification remains UNKNOWN and the next consumer must not read it as verified.

S5. REHEARSAL GATE BEFORE PROPOSING (mandatory).
S5.1 Instantiate the drafted procedure on the frozen episode that supplied the target mechanism, and recompute every prediction from that episode's own fields.
S5.2 Classify each mismatch as transcription/arithmetic (the text is wrong: correct and redraft, no change action) or substantive (the rule is wrong: invoke the stated abandon-or-change action). Carry that split into the falsifier.
S5.3 Recorded precedent to respect: the earlier p3 draft, as written, predicted 0.0166 s against a recorded 0.0129 s (a 37-tick gap) while its design in fact succeeded. That gap is a transcription fault of the prediction form -- reserving boot energy before the threshold crossing and then adding boot delay again double-counts the same interval. A 'deviation beyond a couple of ticks therefore revert' gate would have discarded a correct procedure. So: transcription mismatch corrects the text; only substantive mismatch cancels the rule.
S5.4 ILLUSTRATIVE RECOMPUTATION, not method values -- the numbers below are examples resolved from the frozen world-b records and must be recomputed, never reused, by any consuming run.
 Using the passive-mechanical component record eeb8277f and the single-segment excitation record 219fd490: E_on = 8.624e-5 J; per-tick increment = 6.73e-7 J; n_boot = 129 ticks, so t_boot = 12.9 ms, matching recorded first_boot 0.0129 s exactly; t_ready = 13.9 ms, matching the recorded transmit start; energy after boot = 8.18e-5 J, matching recorded boot energy; t_done = 15.9 ms against the recorded packet at 0.0158 s, i.e. 1 dt tick late, inside tolerance; energy at t_done = 6.61e-5 J versus E_floor = 3.5735e-5 J, margin +3.04e-5 J > 0; peak energy at the end of the powered window = 9.37e-5 J < E_max = 1.1979e-4 J; deadline margin 84.1 ms. Triage: one packet, 8 required bytes, single event id, 0.0158 s <= 0.1 s, so ACHIEVED, and the 0.3395 s brownout prices out as post-terminal. Verdict: all four inequalities hold, S4.1 retains the design, no candidate execution is spent. On the world-p2 fields the same ledger yields packets=[] as a genuine failure whose shunt and dark gap sit inside the capture-to-transmit window, so I1 is violated and no rent reduction of that window is admissible.

S6. UNKNOWN AND COST RULES. Physical calibration, invoice amounts, independent service acceptance and any behavioural claim outside the frozen ideal model are UNKNOWN and stay written as UNKNOWN. An unavailable check is UNKNOWN. Report actual cost as incurred: native calls, bytes, new executions, wall time -- including the three UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE acquisition attempts recorded in S0.2.

S7. RETENTION AND NON-COLLISION. This H supplies no device assignment, no field values for a device, and spends no selection or candidate budget inside the proposal step; it claims no hardware, statistical, transferable or RSI result. Preserve verbatim: p2's three EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT rejections, its misrouted-submission note (the reused-payload retry), and its ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE result; p3's recorded gate miss and its UNKNOWN physical qualification.

S8. CHANNEL DISCIPLINE. Emit exactly one self-contained H proposal carrying this whole text, aimed at the H-proposal channel, needing no follow-up correction to be intelligible or evaluable. If the channel rejects it, record the rejection and output no-update; do not relabel a rejected method as in force.
